title: Barkley puffs split on a long strip at r 0.88: from sparse random patches, puffs bud new puffs into the laminar gaps (18 and 22 persistent splits, generation 2-3, 0 nucleations, 0-2 merges) until the strip is full at ~70 puffs; at r 0.8 they never split, at r 0.895 the strip fills faster
summary: Same world as 20261027T1240-c55-barkley-puffs-sighting on a 16 x 4096 strip with a sparse random start (init_frac 0.03, sigma 0.6). r 0.8 (long_r0.8.png): 16 puffs persist for 3000 t, travel in step and never split or decay, even beside 1000 px of recovered laminar flow. r 0.88 (long_r0.88.png, pack88): puffs repeatedly split, each split leaving two puffs that travel on, and the splitting front invades every laminar gap; labkit seeds 0 and 1: 18 and 22 persistent splits, generation 2 and 3, 43 and 54 persistent tracks, 0 nucleations, 2 and 0 merges; the count rises from 16 to ~71 by t~2000 and then splits nearly stop because the strip is full. r 0.895 (long_r0.895.png): the same, faster (~102 puffs).
limits: Reproduction here is invasion: births happen while there is laminar space and stop when the strip is full, and I saw no puff decays at these parameters, so there is no turnover yet; the published model has decays at lower r, so a regime where splits and decays both happen (or a trait-blind removal) is needed before heredity can be tested. Puffs span the 16 px height (effectively 1D). The 16 x 4096 labkit sheets are hard to read; the space-time panels in long_*.png are the clearer evidence. Two seeds at one r for labkit; screens on seed 0 only; no dt or grid variant.
